correctness.rationale: The genus-defect-one and equality argument reduces all maximal curves with fixed normalization to unique degree-two pinches. Maximal Frobenius is [-p]; difference points form exactly nonzero E[p-1], modulo rational translations. Origin-fixing elliptic automorphisms account for unpointed isomorphisms and branch exchange. The stabilizer order is twice the torsion stabilizer. Burnside fixed-point counts give the complete class and automorphism-order table; the proof covers all primes p>=5 under the stated hypotheses. The included exact checker verifies sample orbit data, weighted mass identities, and point counts of concrete maximal elliptic examples, but does not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The central natural moduli problem is the exact number of nonisomorphic extremal singular genus-two curves with a fixed maximal elliptic normalization, and the distribution of additional automorphisms. The theorem gives a complete uniform census, detects the exact j=0 and j=1728 jumps, and includes all degree-two pinches, not only the interpolated subfamilies in the motivating construction. It is a motivated finite-field isomorphism classification rather than a point-count exercise.
